subject.title: Externally-registered cron jobs auto-enable without user confirmation, inherit expensive default model, no usage circuit breaker

question: Should external, plugin, or agent-origin cron registrations remain enabled by default, or should OpenClaw require provenance-aware explicit activation and model/cost guardrails before recurring model-backed jobs can run?
rationale: Current behavior is confirmed, but changing it affects upgrade compatibility, plugin contracts, operator UX, and security/cost policy in ways automation should not decide unilaterally.

options.title: Add provenance-aware safe defaults
options.body: Require external or agent-origin recurring model-backed jobs to carry trusted provenance and stay disabled or pending confirmation until the operator explicitly enables them, with model/cost warnings before activation.

options.title: Keep enabled default with stronger warnings
options.body: Preserve current compatibility but add doctor/update visibility and documentation so operators see new jobs and inherited model choices before or shortly after registration.

options.title: Split into narrower follow-ups
options.body: Keep cron activation unchanged here and route circuit breaking, cost budgets, and scheduling provenance entirely to #14376, #42475, and #71712.

recommendation.title: Add provenance-aware safe defaults
recommendation.body: Require external or agent-origin recurring model-backed jobs to carry trusted provenance and stay disabled or pending confirmation until the operator explicitly enables them, with model/cost warnings before activation.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter Steinberger is the strongest recent history signal for cron runtime seams and adjacent implementation review, though the final policy decision may require broader maintainer input.
